About Event

​Special Special celebrates its 10th anniversary with an interactive exhibition and new zine exploring the meaning of migration and movement for creatives titled Scenic Route. The exhibition explores Special Special's decade of creative history in the United States’ great “melting pot”. Especially Special is a retrospective, featuring the return of 4N Consulate, a Special Special reading room, and major artist editions from the studio’s archive.

​Opening Thursday, November 19, 6-8PM
on view through December 2, 2026 - RSVP

​40 East 1st St, New York, NY

​

​About Special Special

​Special Special is a New York-based creative studio and platform for unconventional ideas founded by artist Wen-You Cai in 2016. The team includes Panny Chayapumh, Kelly Rogers, and Kenix Xiaoqing Liang.

​For the past ten years, the studio has brought artists and creatives together through exhibitions, publishing, talks, and experimental forms of programming. Working across disciplines and geographies, Special Special creates opportunities for exchange between emerging and established creative voices.

​Special Special believes in the power of a supportive community and making time for connection. Their projects are not optimized for reach, but rather intimacy and warmth. Special Special uses art making as a way to foster true friendships, using projects to establish relationships and open dialogues with a community of creative minds.

​Special Special is a connector, proving that the act of maintaining a creative practice can be an act of art making, in-and-of-itself.

​About 4N

​4N Magazine (sounds like “foreign”) traces creative migration in today’s world. Creativity has no bounds, as creatives seek inspiration wherever it lies in the world, and we desire to highlight its tracks.

​The magazine started in 2024 as a platform for foreign creatives to showcase their work in print, especially for those seeking visas to stay in the US. 4N recognizes the challenges faced by foreigners in obtaining sufficient credentials to demonstrate their value, especially for O-1 and Green Card documentation.

​While similar challenges are posed globally as national alienation grows, 4N continues to build a community-based publication by highlighting the exciting work of international creatives who face the challenges of our ever-changing environment.
